## Control `code`

THE WRITE API: every programmatic read and edit of libraries, controls, facets, commands, flows, scenes, assets, timers/events, tags/groups, plugins, and memory. FLAT returns; journaled where it mutates. This is the surface agents drive.

### dev.code.add_library

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `String` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Create a new library with the given name. With git on PATH the library is born tracked: its data/&lt;lib> is created inside a fresh git repo at repositories/&lt;lib> (the same layout dev.github.import produces) and symlinked into the instance, the repo is registered in the dev.git registry (role library, autocommit on), and the autocommit sweeper makes its first commit within minutes - so canon never sees it and its history starts at creation. Without git it degrades to the plain data/&lt;lib> directory, which the /data/* ignore rule still keeps out of canon.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lib` | String | yes |  |

```bash
  --data-urlencode 'lib=dev' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=jytnoy19ec8a3b50bzff6' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={"lib":"<lib>"}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

### dev.code.check_js

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Checks a JavaScript or TypeScript command without running it: regenerates its files from the store (&lt;lib>/&lt;ctl>/&lt;cmd>.js or .ts with types from the declared params, and flowlang.d.ts), compiles it in V8 as the engine would install it - or, for a command with imports or in TypeScript, bundles it with esbuild, resolving its imports from node_modules next to data/ - and type-checks it with TypeScript's tsc against flowlang.d.ts and the packages' own types when tsc is found ($FLOWLANG_TSC, node_modules/.bin/tsc next to data/, or tsc on the PATH; TypeScript strictly) - names the engine does not provide, such as process or require, are errors, and flowlang.api calls are checked against the callee's declared params. Returns {status, command, tsc: 'ran'|'not installed'|'skipped', clean, problems: [{tool: 'syntax'|'esbuild'|'tsc', severity, where, line, column, message}]} - `where` is the author's own line: 'body line N' or 'imports line N'. clean is false when any problem is an error; status is 'err' only when the check cannot run (not a JavaScript/TypeScript command, a build without javascript_runtime). Use it after upsert_command / patch_command_body on a JavaScript or TypeScript command.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lib` | String | yes |  |
| `ctl` | String | yes |  |
| `cmd` | String | yes |  |

```bash

  "http://localhost:8080/app/exec" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=dev' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=xkjzst1a1a0efa6b8x0' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={"lib":"<lib>","ctl":"<ctl>","cmd":"<cmd>"}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**


### dev.code.convert_patch_journals

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Moves legacy source patch journals (&lt;ctlid>_patches records inside a library) into this instance's local runtime journal, through dev.code.patch_journal's verified migrate path. Select one/all libraries and controls (empty or * = all); limit bounds journals processed (0 unlimited); dry_run reports entries and bytes without writing. Each journal is imported entry by entry, read back and compared, and only then is the legacy record deleted via secured app.delete - in a git-tracked library that shows up as a deleted file to commit. Nothing is written to control records; the runtime journal id is derived from library + control id. Safe to re-run: already-converted journals report already_migrated, and entries an older binary appended to a legacy record after its import are carried over. Returns per-journal results and counts {candidates, converted, entries, skipped, failed}.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lib` | String | yes | One source library, or empty/* for every library with a controls index |
| `ctl` | String | yes | One control name/id, or empty/* for every control in the selected libraries |
| `limit` | Integer | yes | Stop after this many migrated journals; 0 means no limit |
| `dry_run` | Boolean | yes | Report candidate journals without creating or deleting records |
| `nn_sessionid` | String | server | Calling session, used to authorize removal of verified legacy journals |

**HTTP:** `GET /app/exec?lib=dev&id=vxiuon1a1c1872c7ag88&args=…` (via `app.app.exec`)

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/exec" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=dev' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=vxiuon1a1c1872c7ag88' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={"lib":"<lib>","ctl":"<ctl>","limit":0,"dry_run":false}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"exec","params":{"lib":"dev","id":"vxiuon1a1c1872c7ag88","args":{"lib":"<lib>","ctl":"<ctl>","limit":0,"dry_run":false}}}
```

**MCP tool:** `dev-code-convert_patch_journals`

**See also:** [patch_command_body](#devcodepatch_command_body), [patch_control_facet](#devcodepatch_control_facet), [patch_journal](#devcodepatch_journal)

### dev.code.create_control

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** `anonymous` · **Readers:** `["anonymous"]`

Create a new control the journaled way: builds the record with the platform's exact internal shape and registers it in the library's controls index, so patch_control_facet / read_control_facet / delete_control work on it immediately. Refuses to clobber an existing control of the same name. Use this instead of hand-writing data-folder records (which corrupts the index). Returns {status, id, name, lib, created}.

| `lib` | String | yes | Library that will own the new control. |
| `name` | String | yes | Human-facing control name (unique within the library); this is what data-control='lib:name:{}' resolves and what other dev.code commands take as `ctl`. |
| `desc` | String | yes | Optional description; discoverable via list_controls / set_control_meta. |

### dev.code.delete_control

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Deletes a control and everything it owns: its commands (with impl/flow records and their attachments), facets, timer/event components (live listeners deregistered first), its _patches journal, and its entry in the library's controls index. DELETION IS TERMINAL FOR THE JOURNAL - the fine-grained history dies with the control; the canonical repo's git history is the remaining record. Refuses when the control is a published app (name == lib with an _APPS descriptor): unpublish is a separate, deliberate act. `author` is accepted for symmetry with every other mutation; with the journal gone it is recorded nowhere.

### dev.code.find

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `JSONObject` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

STOP WALKING THE FILESYSTEM. The anti-grep / anti-find skill: locate anything in Newbound via the store index or O(1) path math, never by scanning directories or running grep/find over data/ (its mounts can be network-slow). kind=command (a command's source: source_kind=generated reads &lt;lib>/src/&lt;lib>/&lt;ctl>/&lt;cmd>.rs by DIRECT path probe, source_kind=body returns read_command), kind=control (control NAME -> id + sharded path), kind=asset (library asset absolute path), kind=library (list library ids), kind=path (resolve a 16+ char record id to its data/&lt;lib>/[0..4]/[4..8]/[8..12]/[12..16]/&lt;id> location, O(1)), kind=text (search CONTENT: query = one case-insensitive substring run through the global store search dev.search, scoped by lib/ctl - command text, every control facet (html/css/js/memory...), control names/descs and text assets; up to 50 matches {lib, kind, ctl, name, cmd|facet|asset, line, preview}, count = the total; to search the LIVE browser page's visible text use agent.browser.find_text). Pass "" for params a kind does not use. Prefer this over evaluate_rust+read_dir and over shelling out to grep/find.

| `cmd` | String | yes |  |
| `name` | String | yes |  |
| `id` | String | yes |  |
| `source_kind` | String | yes |  |
| `query` | String | yes |  |

### dev.code.patch_command_body

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

The `patch_command_body` command updates the source code of a specific Rust command within a control by replacing a designated code snippet with a new one. It validates the existence of the library, control, command, and implementation file, ensuring the old snippet matches the current code exactly before applying the modification and triggering a recompilation. This operation returns a status object indicating success or providing an error message if the target or snippet cannot be found. Patches apply to the stored code_body — the function body
only, never the generated signature. Preserves the impl record's existing readers/writers across the rewrite (a code edit never resets a gated command to admin-only). JOURNALED on the control's patch journal (facet "command", cmd = the name, op "patch", old/new = the two snippets, compile ok|err) - also when the compile fails, because the store has changed either way; revert = the inverse patch. The result carries patch_id when an entry was written, or journal_warning when the edit landed but could not be journaled. label is the stated reason for the edit, recorded on the entry (the why-harvest pairs it with the change; empty is allowed and records no reason); an empty author defaults to the calling session's user, else anonymous.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lib` | String | yes |  |
| `ctl` | String | yes |  |
| `cmd` | String | yes |  |
| `old_snippet` | String | yes |  |
| `new_snippet` | String | yes |  |
| `label` | String | yes | The stated reason for this edit, recorded on the journal entry (the why-harvest pairs it with the change). May be empty, which records no reason. |
| `author` | String | yes | Who is making the edit, recorded on the journal entry. Empty defaults to the calling session's user, else anonymous. |
| `nn_sessionid` | String | server | Request metadata filled in by the framework; pass an empty string from tools. |

**HTTP:** `GET /app/exec?lib=dev&id=jtlipu19ed5ad4404p2c96&args=…` (via `app.app.exec`)

```bash

  --data-urlencode 'id=jtlipu19ed5ad4404p2c96' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={"lib":"<lib>","ctl":"<ctl>","cmd":"<cmd>","old_snippet":"<old_snippet>","new_snippet":"<new_snippet>","label":"<label>","author":"<author>"}'
```

### dev.code.patch_journal

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Internal shared patch-journal implementation. Patch history is INSTANCE-LOCAL: it lives in the gitignored runtime library as one index record (id DERIVED as dev_journal_&lt;lib>_&lt;ctlid> - nothing is ever written to a tracked record) plus one record per patch. A control with no runtime journal reads its legacy &lt;ctlid>_patches record. ops: read / status (never write); append (first write imports the legacy history into runtime, verified entry by entry, and LEAVES the legacy record alone; never fails on journal state - an unusable index is set aside and a warning returned); migrate (explicit: import, carry over any entries an older binary appended to the legacy record since, then delete the legacy record via app.delete; dry_run reports only); move (re-keys the journal to to_lib after the control has moved and appends the entry); delete. Returns FLAT {status, storage runtime|legacy|none, patches, total, legacy_present, warning...}. Journal writes are serialized per process only. Callers should normally use list_control_patches or convert_patch_journals.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | String | yes | read, status, append, migrate, move, or delete |
| `lib` | String | yes | Source library owning the control |
| `ctl` | String | yes | Source control name or record id |
| `to_lib` | String | yes | Target library for move; empty otherwise |
| `entry` | JSONObject | yes | Patch fields for append/move; empty object otherwise |
| `limit` | Integer | yes | Maximum newest-first patches for read; 0 returns all |
| `dry_run` | Boolean | yes | For migrate: report without writing or deleting |
| `nn_sessionid` | String | server | Calling session; used to authorize legacy/runtime record deletion |

**HTTP:** `GET /app/exec?lib=dev&id=lhynxr1a1c17d987eu46&args=…` (via `app.app.exec`)

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/exec" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=dev' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=lhynxr1a1c17d987eu46' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={"op":"<op>","lib":"<lib>","ctl":"<ctl>","to_lib":"<to_lib>","entry":{},"limit":0,"dry_run":false}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"exec","params":{"lib":"dev","id":"lhynxr1a1c17d987eu46","args":{"op":"<op>","lib":"<lib>","ctl":"<ctl>","to_lib":"<to_lib>","entry":{},"limit":0,"dry_run":false}}}
```

### dev.code.search_commands

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `JSONArray` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Searches all commands for a text query, matching case-insensitively against the command name, parameter names, description, imports, and implementation source. ### dev.code.set_command_imports

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Replaces a text command's file-level import block (the impl record's `import` field) and recompiles. The one section patch_command_body cannot reach: `code_body` is a function body, so file-level `use`/import statements live here. Refuses flow commands. Returns the compile outcome plus old_imports. Preserves the impl record's existing readers/writers across the rewrite. JOURNALED on the control's patch journal (facet "command", cmd = the name, op "imports", old/new = the import blocks, compile ok|err), also when the compile fails; setting the same imports writes no entry. The result carries patch_id when an entry was written, or journal_warning when the edit landed but could not be journaled. label is the stated reason for the edit, recorded on the entry (the why-harvest pairs it with the change; empty is allowed and records no reason); an empty author defaults to the calling session's user, else anonymous.

| `imports` | String | yes |  |

| `author` | String | yes | Who is making the edit, recorded on the journal entry. Empty defaults to the calling session's user, else anonymous. |
| `nn_sessionid` | String | server | Request metadata filled in by the framework; pass an empty string from tools. |

### dev.code.set_groups

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Sets the SECURITY groups on a library, control, or command — a deliberate permission act, distinct from tags (categorization). Empty ctl targets the library's meta.json; empty cmd targets the control record plus its inline data records; else the command's meta and impl records. Writes the comma-delimited groups string AND derives the enforced readers arrays from it (split on comma, trimmed) — the enforcement check_security/check_auth actually read. ### dev.code.trace_flow

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Runs a saved FLOW command once - an ORDINARY run, not a debug session - and reports which root cases of its nextcase chain ran. R5: a thin wrapper over dev.flowstep.run_flow (flowlang's own stepper, the semantics Command::execute runs; no debug session, no tape, no 10k debugger budget, no sentinel nextcase). Returns {status, result, path, cases} plus complete, outcome, end, steps, max_depth, budget, ms, us. result is the envelope a plain run returns (app.app.exec's auth check and format_result; a root terminate is success with the output delivered so far; a failure is {status err, msg, flow_end}). path is [{case, end, op?, ms, us, steps}], one per ROOT case executed, root first, always COMPLETE (nested frames never enter it); end is next (a next rule fired; op = the op), done, terminate, fail, stall, I-4, panic, or budget. ms/us are real monotonic wall time per case measured at the run boundary (nested work is attributed to the root case it ran under). Step budget = the ordinary run's 1,000,000 steps; running out is an explicit budget error (result.flow_end budget). Runs the SAVED body. Inputs: lib, ctl, cmd name the flow command; args are its arguments (JSONObject); nn_sessionid is filled in by the framework (pass "" from javascript). Admin-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lib` | String | yes |  |

| `cmd` | String | yes |  |
| `args` | JSONObject | yes |  |
| `nn_sessionid` | String | server |  |

### dev.code.upsert_command

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

The `upsert_command` command creates or updates a backend command definition within a specified library and control, validating its language, parameters, and return type before persisting the associated Rust code and imports. Upon successful storage, it automatically triggers a compilation process to verify the code's integrity and returns a status object indicating success or detailing any compilation errors. CONTRACT: `code_body` is the FUNCTION BODY ONLY — the system generates `pub fn <cmd>(<params>) -> <return_type>` around it. Never include a fn signature in code_body. Declared params are in scope as named variables of their Rust types. The final expression of code_body must be a value of the declared return_type. Put use statements in `imports`. Updating an existing command preserves its meta and impl records' readers/writers (its security gating); a new command starts admin-only until set_groups grants access. JAVASCRIPT/TYPESCRIPT (lang `javascript` or `typescript`): code_body is the body of a JavaScript function (async when it uses await) whose parameters are the declared params, in order; it ends with `return <value>`, not a final expression. A typescript body may carry type annotations. `imports` holds ES `import` lines for npm packages installed in node_modules next to data/, or for another JavaScript/TypeScript command as `flowlang:<lib>/<ctl>/<cmd>` (its function is the default export; what its imports field exports comes along) - bundled with esbuild; there is no require, process, Buffer or Node built-in. The compile step checks syntax (and bundles imports); run check_js afterwards for the type check. JOURNALED on the control's patch journal (facet "command", cmd = the name, op "create" or "upsert", old/new = the {command, impl} record data as JSON - the shape delete_command journals; old is empty on create), with compile ok|err, also when the compile fails, because the store has changed either way. An upsert that changes nothing writes no entry. The result carries patch_id when an entry was written, or journal_warning when the edit landed but could not be journaled. label is the stated reason for the edit, recorded on the entry (the why-harvest pairs it with the change; empty is allowed and records no reason); an empty author defaults to the calling session's user, else anonymous.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lib` | String | yes |  |
| `ctl` | String | yes |  |
| `cmd` | String | yes |  |
| `lang` | String | yes |  |
| `return_type` | String | yes |  |
| `params` | JSONArray | yes |  |
| `imports` | String | yes |  |
| `code_body` | String | yes |  |
| `label` | String | yes | The stated reason for this edit, recorded on the journal entry (the why-harvest pairs it with the change). May be empty, which records no reason. |
| `author` | String | yes | Who is making the edit, recorded on the journal entry. Empty defaults to the calling session's user, else anonymous. |
| `nn_sessionid` | String | server | Request metadata filled in by the framework; pass an empty string from tools. |

**HTTP:** `GET /app/exec?lib=dev&id=kxljyt19ec8be3066w1038&args=…` (via `app.app.exec`)

```bash
  "http://localhost:8080/app/exec" \
```

### dev.code.write_flow_body

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Stores a flow command's entire body (the Case graph) and records the edit in the control's shared append-only patch journal (facet 'flow', with the command name; revert = write_flow_body of the entry's old body). Creates the flow command when it does not exist (returns created=true); errs if the name belongs to a non-flow command. Optional base hash from read_flow_body ⇒ stale_base on mismatch. Whole-body replace by design: the store re-serializes JSON canonically, so structured whole-body writes are the honest unit; text snippets are not (see the bench's flow3d design, review R-2).

### dev.dev.hard_reset

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** `admin` · **Readers:** `["admin"]`

Hard-reset this instance to canon: hardreset.sh made mechanical as a detached runner sharing the update_crates machinery (same rundir/status file, so the two pipelines mutually refuse to stack; poll dev.dev.update_crates_status, which reports kind:hardreset and steps:6). Steps: (1) guarded git clone of canon into CHUCKTHIS - nothing destructive happens unless the clone succeeds, (2) overlay canon src/data/newbound_core/Cargo.toml over the instance and purge generated sources (Cargo.lock, src/lib.rs, src/{app,dev,peer,security}, cmd; rustup update tolerated-fail), (3) build the canon binary inside the clone, (4) newbound rebuild and (5) newbound recompile THROUGH that canon binary - the new-code-runs-the-rest principle - then the clone is deleted, (6) final feature-matched host build; restart verdict by host-binary hash. Local/overlay libraries are untouched (canon data/* replaces only canon libs). Sets the hotswap_paused gate for the duration. NOTE: FFI crate pins are NOT rewritten - if canon's flowlang/ndata pins moved, crate_versions will report mismatch after restart; run update_crates at the new versions to align them. The instance keeps serving OLD code during the run; avoid store edits while it runs. Callable on a peer via /peer/remote/uuid/dev/hard_reset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | String | yes | Git URL of the canon repo to reset from. Empty string uses the default https://github.com/mraiser/newbound.git. Restricted to [A-Za-z0-9._/:@+-] because it is interpolated into the runner script. |

**HTTP:** `GET /dev/hard_reset`

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/dev/hard_reset" \
  --data-urlencode 'url=<url>'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"dev","cmd":"hard_reset","params":{"url":"<url>"}}
```

**MCP tool:** `dev-dev-hard_reset`

**See also:** [crate_versions](#devdevcrate_versions), [update_crates](#devdevupdate_crates)

### dev.dev.restart_instance

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `String` · **Groups:** `admin` · **Readers:** `["admin"]`

Restart THIS Newbound instance, however it was launched - /proc/self/cgroup dispatch: a system systemd unit gets systemctl --no-block restart (sudo -n when not root), a user unit gets systemctl --user --no-block restart, and a plain command-line/session process self-respawns (a detached watcher waits for this pid to exit, then execs the identical cmdline in the identical cwd; output to runtime/restart.log). Returns OK/ERROR from the exit status before the process dies. Linux-only. NOTE: the command restarts the PROCESS THAT EXECUTES IT - called over the MCP bridge it restarts the MCP child, not the HTTP instance; call it through the HTTP instance (UI, /dev/restart_instance, or a peer's /peer/remote/uuid/dev/restart_instance).

### dev.dev.update_crates

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** `admin` · **Readers:** `["admin"]`

Update the platform's flowlang/ndata crate versions. Step 0 runs in-process: rewrite the pins in every manifest in lockstep (root, newbound_core, cmd, all FFI crate roots; each line's =-pin style preserved) and set the in-memory hotswap_paused gate. Everything else runs through the NEW code via a detached command-line runner (/bin/sh in its own process group, logged): (1) cargo build feature-matched to this instance, (2) newbound rebuild, (3) newbound recompile, (4) final cargo build - restart verdict by host-binary hash before/after. Refuses an ndata bump without a flowlang bump (ndata rides flowlang releases; the hotswap ABI-contract guard keys on the flowlang version) and refuses to stack runs. Poll dev.dev.update_crates_status for progress and the verdict; equal-to-current versions are allowed as a repair re-run. Callable on a peer via /peer/remote/uuid/dev/update_crates.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flowlang` | String | yes | The flowlang crate version to pin (e.g. 0.3.35). May equal the current version to re-run the pipeline as a repair. |
| `ndata` | String | yes | The ndata crate version to pin (e.g. 0.3.18). An ndata change without a flowlang change is refused: ndata rides flowlang releases, and the hotswap ABI-contract guard keys on the flowlang version. |

**HTTP:** `GET /dev/update_crates`

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/dev/update_crates" \
  --data-urlencode 'flowlang=<flowlang>' \
  --data-urlencode 'ndata=<ndata>'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"dev","cmd":"update_crates","params":{"flowlang":"<flowlang>","ndata":"<ndata>"}}
```

**MCP tool:** `dev-dev-update_crates`

**See also:** [crate_versions](#devdevcrate_versions), [hard_reset](#devdevhard_reset), [update_crates_status](#devdevupdate_crates_status)

### dev.dev.update_crates_status

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** `admin` · **Readers:** `["admin"]`

Poll the runner launched by dev.dev.update_crates OR dev.dev.hard_reset (they share one rundir/status file and refuse to stack): FLAT {state: none|running|stalled|failed|done, step, label, verdict: restart|no-restart|'', pid, time, hotswap_paused, log_tail} plus, on hard-reset runs, steps (6) and kind (hardreset) - crate updates count 0-4. Detects a runner that died without reporting (pid check -> stalled). Clears the in-memory hotswap_paused gate ONLY on a clean no-restart finish; a restart verdict or a failed/stalled run keeps the gate set (new-ABI dylibs must not load into this host) until the restart clears it inherently.

No parameters.

**HTTP:** `GET /dev/update_crates_status`

## Control `flowstep`

Flow step debugger for flowlang flows (spec: dev/_ASSETS/docs/flow-language.md section 1.5.4). CORE (P1/P2): step(state, pick) -> (state', event), a ready-set stepper over a frame stack (local/flow-command frames, list/loop iterations), one event per step; run/drive continue it under a pick policy or step mode (over/out/run_to); validate checks every event's preconditions; parity compares a run against Code::execute. DEBUG SESSIONS (P3): debug_start(lib, ctl, cmd, body, args) opens an in-memory session (an unsaved editor body is allowed) with a recorded tape - each step with its inverse, a snapshot every 64 steps, persistent globals captured/restored, side-effecting command ops flagged; debug_step(session, mode, pick) does into/over/out/run_to/continue (own thread, pause flag, step budget)/pause/back/goto/edit/reexecute/branch - forward after back replays, an alternate pick/edit/reexecute forks a branch; debug_state, debug_set_breakpoints (op, wire, sync, case, rule; stall/error always stop), debug_stop; debug_reap (timer reap_debug_sessions, every 5 min) drops sessions idle 30 min. Admin-only.

### dev.flowstep.debug_reap

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Flow step debugger (P3, lifecycle R4): timer target (every 5 minutes, the control's reap timer). Ends IDLE debug sessions with no debug_* call and no step for 30 minutes (tombstoned, so a later stop/state answers ended_by reap). Never unlinks a session that has an owner: a running continue refreshes its heartbeat every step, so it stays alive without HTTP polls; an owner whose heartbeat is older than 2 hours (one op executing that long) is ASKED to stop (phase stopping) and ends itself at its next step boundary - the op in flight completes and is recorded once. Returns {status, removed: [ids], stopping: [ids], kept, workers (live continue threads), ended (tombstones)}. Admin-only.

Flow step debugger P3: debug_set_breakpoints(session, list) replaces a debug session's breakpoints. Entries: {kind: op|wire|sync, index, frame?, case?} stops BEFORE that item is picked (op = before its eval/enter, wire = before delivery); {kind: case, case, frame?} stops right after the case is entered (seed); {kind: rule, rule?, op?, case?, frame?} stops after the eval that fired a rule, before its effect. frame = path [[op, iter], ...] ([] = root; absent = any). Stall and error always stop. Applies to over/out/run_to/continue, replayed and executed steps alike; a run never stops on the breakpoint it starts from. Returns {status, session, breakpoints}. ### dev.flowstep.debug_start

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Flow step debugger P3: open a debug session on flow command lib.ctl.cmd. debug_start(lib, ctl, cmd, body, args) -> {status, session, cursor 0, hash, boundary, ...}. body = the root Case JSON to debug - an UNSAVED editor body is allowed; pass {} to debug the saved body. args = the flow's arguments (raw, no cast_params; copied once, aliases among them kept). The session lives in memory (globals.flowstep_debug) until debug_stop or the idle reaper (debug_reap timer, 30 min). Drive it with debug_step (into/over/out/run_to/continue/back/goto/edit/branch/pause), inspect with debug_state, set breakpoints with debug_set_breakpoints. SESSION BOUNDARY (returned as `boundary`): persistent globals are NOT isolated - the session reads and writes the real process globals, the same handles an ordinary run uses; back/goto/replay overwrite them with the tape's values, and a concurrent ordinary run or another session writing the same persistent key is neither detected nor undone, so debug persistent flows where nothing else writes those keys. rust/python command ops are opaque: their outside effects are flagged (side_effects, crossed_side_effects), never undone. Admin-only.

### dev.flowstep.debug_step

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Flow step debugger P3 session engine: debug_step(session, mode, pick) moves a debug session (from debug_start) along its recorded TAPE and returns {status, session, mode, cursor, base, length, event, ready, default, ended, depth, phase, running, hash, tape_hash, branches, ...}. Every executed step is recorded with its inverse (a structural change list {p, o, n}), the persistent-global changes, its view and a canonical state hash; a full snapshot every 64 steps; tape capped (50k steps / 4M nodes, oldest 64-blocks dropped). modes: into = one step; over / out = P2 drive's unit rules; run_to = until the next default pick is pick.target {kind: wire|sync|op, index, frame?, case?}; reexecute = one step, forcing execution (forks); continue = to the end on its OWN THREAD (returns at once with running true; pick.budget, default 10000; pick.wait true joins) - stops at breakpoints, pause, stop, budget, or the end; pause = ask the running owner to stop at its next step boundary; stop = end the session (debug_stop; pick.wait_ms bounds the wait, default 10000); reap = the idle reaper (debug_reap); back (pick.count, default 1) / goto (pick.seq) = roll back or forward without executing, restoring persistent globals (crossed_side_effects lists opaque rust/python command steps passed backwards: rollback restores the interpreter, not the world); edit = set a value at pick.path ["frames", i, "inputs"|"results"|"out"|"args", ...] to pick.value as an undoable tape step; branch = at a branch's fork point, swap the tape tail with recorded branch pick.id; state = the full view (debug_state). Stepping forward where the tape continues REPLAYS it (replayed counts, nothing executes) while the requested item (pick {kind, index}, or {} = the default) is the one the tape took; another ready item, edit or reexecute FORKS - the old tail is kept as a branch record (max 16). Pick for into/over/out/continue: {} = default, {kind, index} = a READY item (anything else is refused, state unchanged). R4 LIFECYCLE: phase idle | running | pausing | stopping, then terminal (unlinked from globals.flowstep_debug; a tombstone in globals.flowstep_debug_ended, max 64 / 6 h, answers later calls: stop -> ok already:true, state/step -> err phase stopped, ended_by stop|reap). Exactly ONE owner moves the tape: every mutating mode (synchronous call, or the continue worker - the claim moves into its thread) claims idle -> running and is refused while another owner holds it; only the owner leaves running (idle, or the terminal cleanup when stop/reap asked for stopping meanwhile). Each claim has a fresh run token, so a stale owner cannot write last_run, clear running on a newer run, or resurrect an ended session; ids come from a process counter and are never recycled. Pause and stop are COOPERATIVE at step boundaries: the owner checks before EVERY step; an op already executing (rust/python/user code) cannot be preempted - it completes and is recorded exactly once, then the owner stops (latency = the remaining time of that one op). stop waits for the owner's acknowledgement and only then reports stopped/acknowledged true (else acknowledged:false, phase stopping, and the owner ends the session itself after the op). The worker writes a heartbeat (beat) every step, so an active continue is never reaped for lack of HTTP polls; the reaper ends idle sessions after 30 min and only ASKS an owner whose heartbeat is older than 2 h to stop. A static lock guards only these transitions, never a step or user code (scratch.skills.flowstep_r4_check). Robustness: a tape change or alias group that no longer matches the state's shape is REFUSED (status err, or stopped "refused: ..." mid-run) with the session's cur, cursor and persistent globals left as they were - never a panic midway; alias links that would put a container inside itself are refused; every state walk (hash, size, diff) is cycle-safe (back-reference marker @cycle) and depth-capped at 256, and alias identity is keyed by (object|array, ref) since ndata's object and array heaps number independently. R3 alias carriage: the interpreter&lt;->persistent-global aliasing at each cursor is recorded on every tape entry (xafter), edit step and snapshot (x), so an execution after goto/replay, at a cap-TRIMMED base, or after an edit relinks the very handles an ordinary run shares (an edit detaches only the edited path). Persistent globals are NOT isolated from other writers - see debug_start's boundary. REPLY EVENT LISTS (R6): `event` is always the tape's step cursor-1 with its seq; `events` lists a move's executed/replayed steps in seq order - into/over/out/run_to/reexecute/continue - and holds at most the FIRST 400 (events_truncated true; goto reaches every step); edit, back, goto and branch replies carry only `event`. Every listed event has a numeric seq equal to its tape index, strictly increasing (scratch.skills.flowstep_r3_seq_check, flowstep_r6_timeline_check). Admin-only; no auth checks inside. R3 D1 alias split/join: a step that re-points a path that was one of several aliases or joins two separate containers is marked tx on its tape entry (txp = example paths); every move crossing a tx entry detaches the restored copy before applying and links the arrival cursor's alias groups (scratch.skills.flowstep_r3_split_check). Persistent keys get the same treatment. Limitation: the canonical state hash ignores everything deeper than 256 levels, so two states that differ only below that depth hash equal - matching hashes there prove nothing; the change lists still carry those values. R3 D2 command bodies: a command frame's body (the callee's SAVED flow, loaded at enter) is stored once per command AND content hash, so a callee re-saved mid-session keeps every frame's OWN body across goto/replay/fork (scratch.skills.flowstep_r3_d2_check). Graph-body contents never enter diff; a changed command body is a new $body ref.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session` | String | yes |  |
| `mode` | String | yes |  |
| `pick` | JSONObject | yes |  |

### dev.flowstep.debug_stop

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Flow step debugger (P3, lifecycle R4): debug_stop(session) ends a debug session. Idle session: ended at once. Session with an owner (a running continue or a synchronous step): marked stopping; the owner finishes the op in flight - stop is COOPERATIVE, an executing rust/python/user op cannot be preempted and is recorded exactly once - then sees stopping at the step boundary, runs no further step and does the terminal cleanup itself; this call waits up to 10 s for that acknowledgement. Returns {status ok, session, stopped, acknowledged, already, was_running, phase, ended_by, cursor, length, waited_ms}; stopped/acknowledged are true ONLY once the owner has acknowledged (else phase stopping, acknowledged false, msg - the owner ends the session after its op). Idempotent and race-safe: concurrent stops (editor stop + dispose) or a stop racing the reaper all wait for the same single cleanup; a stop of an already stopped/reaped session answers ok with already:true from its tombstone (64 kept, 6 h). Persistent globals stay as they are at the session's final cursor. Admin-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session` | String | yes |  |

### dev.flowstep.drive

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Step modes over step (flow step debugger P2): drive(state, mode, pick, target, budget) -> {status, mode, stopped, steps, ended, depth, ready, default, event, events, state}. mode: into = one step; over = one step, and if it opened a unit (pushed a frame, started a list/loop op, or began an iteration) continue until that unit closed (a frame: its leave AND the enclosing op's closing eval); out = finish the innermost open unit (the op in progress in the top frame; else the top nested frame through its enclosing op's closing eval; in the root with nothing in progress, to the end); run_to = continue until the next DEFAULT pick is target {kind: wire|sync|op, index} (optional frame path [[op,iter],...] and case) - a breakpoint, it stops BEFORE the item runs; continue = to the end. ### dev.flowstep.run_flow

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

### dev.flowstep.step

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Flow step debugger core with FRAMES (P2; spec: dev/_ASSETS/docs/flow-language.md 1.5.4). step(state, pick) -> {status, state, event, ready, default, ended, depth}: advances a flow ONE step over a frame stack and emits one event (enter, seed, deliver, sync, iter, eval, leave, next, terminate, fail, finish, done, stall, error). Start with state = {body: the flow's root Case JSON, args}, then pass back the returned state {body, frames, seq}; graphs are never mutated, the stepper's bookkeeping is copied per step and value handles are shared (flowlang aliasing). Local ops with localdata and command ops whose callee is a flow (any library; raw args, no auth re-check - the parent call is the gate) open a frame: enter ... leave, then the op's closing eval (a fail inside becomes b=false at the caller's condition; command outputs map by position). List/loop ops run as iterations: iter, then one eval or enter..leave+eval; the last iteration's eval carries done and the collected outputs; finish stops a loop only via a local frame's finish flag. rust/python command ops stay one opaque eval. Only the top frame steps and an op in progress is atomic (ready = [{kind:auto}]). pick = {} takes the DEFAULT pick (flowlang's sweep order, so continuing with {} is the Code::execute run); {kind: wire|sync|op, index} picks a READY item of the top frame - anything else is refused with status err and the state unchanged. No re-run (a second delivery is reported as I-1); I-4 gives an error event, a stuck case a stall event. An error or stall event ends the WHOLE run on its own step even when a NESTED frame emitted it (the crate's terminal rule, as in flowlang::stepper::run): that reply has ended=true and the root is ended in the returned state, so no residual step is ever taken or recorded (no synthetic 'the run has already ended' event; scratch.skills.flowstep_r6_nested_fatal_check). Depth limit 64 frames. Step modes (over/out/run_to) are in drive.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | JSONObject | yes |  |
| `pick` | JSONObject | yes |  |

## Control `git`

Git as a first-class platform surface: the repo registry (runtime/dev/repos.json) plus mode-split wrappers (read / write / remote_op) over one no-shell argv engine that honors git's exit status, the branch workflow as compound commands (repo_state: the one state sentence vs upstream AND vs origin/master; start_branch from origin's master, published at birth; update_from_master; merge_to_master; abandon_branch with discard and a next branch), and the sweeper (autocommit_sweep: fetch every repo, commit + push autocommit repos, never on master/main). Its html/css/js facets are the workflow panel: one state line per repo (uncommitted / unpushed / not in master / master moved) and five verbs - start branch, update from master, merge → master, abandon, more (the atomic git surface: status, store, log, diff, commit, commit unit, publish, push, fetch, registry edit/remove).

### dev.git.abandon_branch

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

"This is bad - drop this branch and start over from master." Guarded destructive workflow. A dirty tree or a merge in flight is REFUSED unless discard=true, which runs merge --abort / reset --hard HEAD / clean -fd so no edit and no new store record survives. Then checkout the default branch (master, else main) -> branch -D &lt;branch> -> (delete_remote=true) push origin --delete &lt;branch>; origin's copy is KEPT by default, so an abandon is recoverable from the remote -> when next_branch is non-empty, dev.git.start_branch takes over (fetch, fast-forward default to origin, cut, publish) and the result rides under `next`; otherwise the default branch is fetched and fast-forwarded to origin's in place. Refuses the default branch itself or a nonexistent branch; the mutating-command confirm gate is the 'are you sure?' by mechanism. Returns {status, msg, abandoned, now_on, discarded, remote_deleted, next, steps}.

### dev.git.autocommit_sweep

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

The sweeper (normally fired by its 5-minute timer) - the whole 'save' step made mechanical. For EVERY registered repo with an origin it runs fetch --prune, so repo_state's and the git sensor's ahead/behind numbers are real without a click. For repos flagged autocommit it stages and commits when the tree is dirty, then pushes whenever the branch tracks a remote and holds anything unpushed (an unpublished branch is reported, not published). NEVER commits on master/main: 'branches always' is enforced here (result refused_default_branch), for every repo alike. A clean tree, a git-less box, or an absent registry is a free no-op. Returns {swept, committed, pushed, fetched, results:[{repo, fetched, branch, result, paths, push, ...}]}.

No parameters.

### dev.git.carry_branch

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

"My commits landed on master/main" - the recovery for a repo that autocommitted onto its default branch before the 'branches always' rule: move those commits onto a new branch and put the local default back where origin has it, without touching the working tree. fetch --prune -> checkout -b &lt;branch> at the default's current HEAD -> branch -f &lt;default> origin/&lt;default> (a pointer move, never a checkout) -> push -u origin &lt;branch>. Nothing is rewritten and nothing force-pushed: the commits keep their history under the new name; run update_from_master afterwards to fold in what origin gained meanwhile (behind_base says how much). Requires origin, being ON the default branch, and at least one commit origin/&lt;default> lacks (otherwise: start_branch). Refuses an existing branch name, conflicts, a merge in flight. Uncommitted edits ride along untouched (carried). Returns {status, msg, branch, default, base, carried_commits, behind_base, published, publish_err, carried, steps}.

### dev.git.gitrun

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Internal engine for dev.git.{read,write,remote_op}: probes git availability once per process (cached PATH scan - a git-less box gets a plain 'git is not installed' err, never a spawn failure), resolves the repo name in runtime/dev/repos.json, enforces the per-mode verb allowlist, builds argv (git --no-optional-locks -C &lt;path> &lt;verb> &lt;args...>), and makes ONE spawn - no shell, nothing interpolated. ### dev.git.merge_to_master

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

"This is working now" — merge the current feature branch into the repo's default branch (local master, else main) and push it upstream, then return to the feature branch. Transactional: requires that you are ON the branch being merged, no conflicts, no merge in flight; checkout default → merge --no-ff → push origin &lt;default> → checkout back, bailing with the step's stderr on any failure. A dirty tree is NOT a blocker: git itself refuses a checkout or merge that would overwrite an edit (gitrun reports the refusal verbatim and the command steps back to the branch with nothing changed), and edits it does not touch ride along untouched, reported as `carried` (Cargo.lock, rewritten by every build, is the standing case). A real merge conflict is reported with the tree left mid-merge on the default branch (resolve then commit, or dev.git merge --abort) — never silently half-merged. Returns {status, msg, branch, default, carried, steps}.

|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | String | yes |  |
| `branch` | String | yes |  |

### dev.git.start_branch

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

"Start a new working branch from master." Compound and transactional: fetch --prune -> checkout the default branch (master, else main) -> merge --ff-only origin/&lt;default> (a diverged local default is an error to see, never papered over) -> checkout -b &lt;branch> -> push -u origin &lt;branch>. ### dev.git.untrack_generated

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Repos under repositories/ never track builder-generated files: &lt;crate>/src/api.rs is regenerated by every rebuild to mirror the libraries on THIS box, and &lt;crate>/Cargo.lock resolves THIS box's dependency tree - shipping either dirties every other instance's checkout after its first build. Makes a repo conform, as mechanism: git rm --cached every tracked Cargo.lock and src/api.rs (files stay on disk), appends an anchored ignore line for each crate's pair (a crate = a directory holding a tracked Cargo.toml, the root included) that git does not already ignore (check-ignore), commits with `message` (empty = a standard message), pushes when the branch tracks a remote. Idempotent: a conforming repo answers ok with committed:false. Refuses the instance's own checkout, decided by PATH (registry path == instance root), never by role: its workspace Cargo.lock and newbound_core/src/api.rs are tracked on purpose. Also refuses master/main (branches always - start_branch or carry_branch first), a merge in flight, and a non-empty index (pre-staged work would ride into the commit). Returns {status, msg, branch, untracked:[paths], ignored:[lines], committed, pushed, push_err, steps}.

Uninstall a git-imported library: deactivates its app, unlinks the data/runtime (and FFI crate) symlinks - refusing to touch real directories - and deletes repositories/&lt;lib> only when delete_repository is true. Local runtime state (keys, networks) lives under that clone, so delete_repository=true destroys it; false keeps the clone for the user to dispose of. Restart to unload compiled commands.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lib` | String | yes |  |
| `delete_repository` | Boolean | yes |  |

**HTTP:** `GET /app/exec?lib=dev&id=tzouzo19fe778ea1ap2&args=…` (via `app.app.exec`)

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/exec" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=dev' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=tzouzo19fe778ea1ap2' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={"lib":"<lib>","delete_repository":false}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"exec","params":{"lib":"dev","id":"tzouzo19fe778ea1ap2","args":{"lib":"<lib>","delete_repository":false}}}
```

**MCP tool:** `dev-github-remove`

## Control `plugins`

The plugin registry's home: list_plugins reads runtime/dev/plugins.json ({name: {target_lib, target_ctl, plugin_lib, plugin_ctl, selector}}); set_plugin/remove_plugin (dev.code) edit it. The PASS lives in api.js's installControl: after any control activates, entries targeting it install at selector (scoped to the control's element) or, selectorless, into a hidden div appended to it — a headless payload riding the target's lifecycle. Hosts embed nothing; entries apply on the next page load.

### dev.plugins.available

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `JSONObject` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Lists every plugin that declares itself in the store, for the shelf's plugins dropdown. A control meant to be mounted as a plugin carries a `plugin` facet: JSON text {name?, target_lib, target_ctl, selector, desc?} giving its default registration (or an array of those for more than one home); name defaults to &lt;lib>-&lt;ctl>. Walks every library's controls index and probes each control's &lt;id>.plugin attachment (one stat per control; no record is read). Takes no input. Returns {plugins:[{name, plugin_lib, plugin_ctl, target_lib, target_ctl, selector, desc, registered (this instance's runtime/dev/plugins.json already mounts this plugin at this target and selector), registered_as (that entry's name), name_taken (the declared name is used by a different registration)}] sorted by plugin, errors:[{lib, ctl, msg}] for declarations that are malformed or incomplete}. Read-only; register one with dev.code.set_plugin.

No parameters.

**HTTP:** `GET /app/exec?lib=dev&id=wmvwzt1a1e0c79731g0&args=…` (via `app.app.exec`)

```bash
  --data-urlencode 'lib=dev' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=wmvwzt1a1e0c79731g0' \
```

## Control `search`

Global text search over the store: one trigram mask per record (control meta, every text facet, command source, text assets), kept in a flat instance-local index per library under runtime/dev/search/. query prunes by mask, verifies against the live record, and answers store identities with line previews; index rebuilds; status reports.

### dev.search.index

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Rebuilds the global search index for one library (or every library when lib is "" or "*"): one trigram mask per document - each control's name+desc, every text facet on the control record, each command's searchable text (name, desc, imports, parameter names, source), and each text asset (UTF-8, at most 2 MB) - written as ONE flat file runtime/dev/search/&lt;lib>.idx (instance-local; tmp + rename). Doc masks are sized to their content (16 bits per distinct byte trigram of the lowercased text, power of two, capped at 2^17 bits); the file head carries a 2^20-bit library mask so a query can rule a library out from the header alone. No third-party crates. Returns FLAT {status, dir, libraries:[{lib, docs, bytes, ms} or {lib, error}]}. Also the home of the dev.search kernel (module-level pub fns: trigram_hashes, build, load, header, collect, doc_text, command_text, search, lib_ids). File layout (NBSRCH02): magic, built ms, fingerprint, doc count, library mask, watch list, docs. FRESHNESS: the watch list names every file the index was built from (record files and their id-prefixed attachment siblings, relative to data/&lt;lib>); the fingerprint covers their mtimes and sizes plus every asset's. dev.search.query calls ensure_fresh per library (stats only, at most once per 2 s per process) and rebuilds a missing or stale index itself, so this command is only needed to force a rebuild. Also exports collect_ids, watch_paths, fingerprint, read_watch, is_fresh, ensure_fresh.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lib` | String | yes | Library to (re)index. Pass "" or "*" to rebuild every library's index. |

**HTTP:** `GET /app/exec?lib=dev&id=jiyqtw1a1d0627554g1&args=…` (via `app.app.exec`)

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/exec" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=dev' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=jiyqtw1a1d0627554g1' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={"lib":"<lib>"}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"exec","params":{"lib":"dev","id":"jiyqtw1a1d0627554g1","args":{"lib":"<lib>"}}}
```

**MCP tool:** `dev-search-index`

**See also:** [query](#devsearchquery), [status](#devsearchstatus)

### dev.search.query

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Global text search over the store. query is ONE case-insensitive substring (spaces included). Searches control names/descs, every text facet (html, css, js, memory, ...), command text (name, desc, imports, parameter names, source) and text assets, across every library or scoped by lib / ctl / kinds (comma-separated subset of control,facet,command,asset; "" = all). Each library's flat index (runtime/dev/search/&lt;lib>.idx, built on demand when missing) rules out records by trigram mask; every surviving candidate is then VERIFIED against the live record, so a hit is always true. FRESHNESS: each index remembers the files it was built from (record files, their attachment siblings, assets) with a fingerprint of their mtimes and sizes; before a library is searched those files are re-statted (no record is read; at most once per 2 s per library per process) and the library is rebuilt when anything moved (counted in indexes_built), so edits by any writer - dev.code commands, git, another process - are found by the next query, at worst 2 s late. Each hit is filtered by the session's read access to its record (security check_auth, as app.app.read; assets are public like app.app.asset). Returns FLAT {status, query, count (total), truncated, pruned_by_mask (false for queries under 3 bytes: full read), libraries_searched, libraries_ruled_out, indexes_built, candidates, denied, ms, matches:[{lib, kind, ctl, name, cmd|facet|asset, line (first matching line), preview (up to 3 matching lines), changed_since_index}]}.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lib` | String | yes | Library to search; "" or "*" = every library. |
| `ctl` | String | yes | Control to search within; "" or "*" = every control. Naming a control excludes assets, which belong to the library. |
| `kinds` | String | yes | Comma-separated subset of control,facet,command,asset; "" = all four. |
| `query` | String | yes | One case-insensitive substring, spaces included (not a word list). Under 3 bytes it cannot use the masks and every record is read. |
| `limit` | Integer | yes | Maximum matches returned (count still reports the total); &lt;=0 means 50. |
| `nn_sessionid` | String | server | Request metadata filled in by the framework; every hit is filtered by this session's read access to the record. |

**HTTP:** `GET /app/exec?lib=dev&id=jggqph1a1d062caa1u3&args=…` (via `app.app.exec`)

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/exec" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=dev' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=jggqph1a1d062caa1u3' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={"lib":"<lib>","ctl":"<ctl>","kinds":"<kinds>","query":"<query>","limit":0}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"exec","params":{"lib":"dev","id":"jggqph1a1d062caa1u3","args":{"lib":"<lib>","ctl":"<ctl>","kinds":"<kinds>","query":"<query>","limit":0}}}
```

**MCP tool:** `dev-search-query`

**See also:** [index](#devsearchindex), [status](#devsearchstatus)
